title: Integration kickoff: Edge gateway + SDKs - HelioForge
meeting_header: Date: 2029-04-12 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: 7 | Recording: available in Fireflies
summary: Initial integration kickoff to evaluate Redwood options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for HelioForge's edge gateway use case. Main asks: SDK support (Python/Go), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, proxy/gateway placement, per-tenant rate limits and quota model, observability hooks and traceability into their APM, and security (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a small perf benchmark and provide security docs and example LangChain adapter. Next step: pilot proposal and pricing outline.
topics: SDKs: python/go/js support and example clients
Observability hooks: traces, token-level metrics, error traces
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs: latency, data residency, control
action_items: Arielle Gomez: Send pricing comparison matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and pilot SOW draft (due: 2029-04-15)
Marcus Lee: Share a sample LangChain adapter repo and LlamaIndex prompt templates (due: 2029-04-16)
Diane Huang: Provide benchmarking checklist and recommended synthetic workload for edge gateway test (due: 2029-04-17)
Elena Park (HelioForge): Share SOC2 questions and any existing compliance checklist (due: 2029-04-16)
next_steps: Redwood to deliver security pack + SOC2 summary link
Set up a 2-week dedicated pilot on Redwood Dedicated with 2 GPU nodes for HelioForge edge gateway tests
Schedule pilot kickoff w/ infra and security week of 2029-04-22
HelioForge to provide sample traffic patterns and per-tenant QPS distribution by 2029-04-18
transcript:
0:00 Arielle Gomez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Arielle from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We also have Marcus from the SE team and Diane from solutions. Quick roll call?
0:07 Tomás Rivera: Hi Tomás here, CTO at HelioForge. Priya and Jared here too.
0:12 Priya Menon: Priya, lead ML.
0:14 Jared Kwan: Jared, infra.
0:15 Elena Park: Elena, security.
0:18 Arielle Gomez: Awesome. Quick agenda: integration options (SDKs, connectors), gateway placement for edge routing, quotas/rate limit model and observability. We'll talk hosted vs dedicated vs private, and propose next steps. Does that sound good?
0:27 Tomás Rivera: Yep that's perfect. We're trying to decide whether we can use Redwood Hosted for most of our inference needs vs needing Dedicated or Private for data residency and latency for our EU customers.
0:36 Marcus Lee: Great. Maybe I'll kick off with SDK support and typical integration patterns. We support first-class SDKs in Python, Node and Go. There are also prebuilt adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex, and a gateway proxy pattern we often recommend for multi-tenant routing.
0:52 Priya Menon: Are those adapters maintained upstream? We prefer an opinionated example but we will fork. Curious how close they are to what we'd use in production.
1:03 Marcus Lee: Most are in our github examples org; they are maintained by developer experience, but we treat them as examples not prod products. We'll walk you through how to extend them — for example there is a LangChain chain wrapper, and an index connector for LlamaIndex. Note sometimes the docs show "Lamda" adapter — sorry, typo — I mean LangChain.
1:20 Priya Menon: Haha, I saw a doc that referenced lamda once, had me confused.
1:24 Arielle Gomez: On the gateway/proxy question: customers either put a sidecar next to their service instances (low latency per-call) or a central gateway that handles routing, batching and per-tenant quotas. For edge scenarios with lots of regional traffic, the sidecar + local route to a nearby Redwood Dedicated pool often works well.
1:45 Jared Kwan: So if we do sidecar, we run the proxy in our k8s cluster? That would then call Redwood's hosted endpoints? Or does the sidecar talk to a dedicated pool directly? We want to minimize egress and keep hop count low.
1:58 Marcus Lee: Both are possible. Sidecar can call Hosted endpoints through a VPC egress path, or the sidecar can authenticate directly to a Dedicated pool if you provision a private network peering/VPC connection. For Private deployments (on-prem or air-gapped), the proxy can remain entirely internal. Each has tradeoffs in terms of control and maintenance.
2:16 Elena Park: On the compliance side, what's the encryption story and KMS options? We need customer-managed keys for EU data.
2:24 Diane Huang: We support CMK via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted also supports envelope encryption but CMK for hosted is an enterprise add-on. We'll share details in the security pack. For private deployments you get full KMS control.
2:40 Tomás Rivera: Good. Next: rate limits and quotas. We have multi-tenant workloads — per-customer quotas matter. Can Redwood do per-tenant token quotas and throttling in the gateway or is that something we must implement?
2:55 Marcus Lee: Redwood has per-api-key quotas and route-level rate limits. Typical pattern: you front Redwood with your gateway that enforces per-tenant billing quotas, and Redwood enforces global per-key throttles. We also offer token-level metrics and can plug into your quota service via webhooks for near-real-time billing signals. There can be a small propagation lag depending on config.
3:20 Priya Menon: When you say token-level metrics, can we get per-request latency histograms and token counts streamed into our APM? We need fine-grained observability for model regressions.
3:33 Diane Huang: Yes — we provide metric hooks and a tracing integration. We emit request traces, token counts, model variant, and latency percentiles. Those can be exported to Datadog/New Relic or pulled via our observability API. For Dedicated/Private, you also get lower-level GPU-level telemetry.
3:50 Jared Kwan: How heavy is the observability telemetry? We're worried about the cost of exporting token-by-token logs.
3:58 Marcus Lee: Good question. We recommend sampling for token-level traces; by default we emit aggregate per-request counters and per-route histograms. Token-level streaming is opt-in and is typically used for troubleshooting or eval windows. We can show you the cost tradeoffs.
4:13 Tomás Rivera: Performance — we want 95th p50 latencies under 120ms for short prompts (~64 tokens) for EU users. Any data on that?
4:23 Marcus Lee: With a Dedicated pool and optimized kernels we can hit 50–100ms p95 for small requests on modern A100/H100 classes, depending on batching and KV cache warmness. Hosted can be close but depends on noisy-neighbor and region placement. We'll propose a Dedicated pilot so you can run real traffic.
4:45 Priya Menon: For our use case we're doing a lot of retrieval-augmented generation; sessions are chatty and KV cache use matters. How does Redwood handle prefix caching and long conversation contexts?
4:58 Marcus Lee: We do automatic KV cache management for LRU key eviction and prefix caching optimizations; you can configure churn policies. For RAG, we often push retrieval outputs as context windows and use continuous batching to keep latency predictable. Note sometimes in transcripts or docs the term "K V cache" gets spelled out weirdly, that is our cache for key/value attention states.
5:20 Elena Park: On authentication: we require SSO, SAML, and RBAC integration, and audit logs for all requests. Can Redwood support that?
5:30 Diane Huang: Yes. Hosted supports SCIM/SSO for enterprise tenants and audit logs via our retention add-on. Dedicated/Private gives you admin-level RBAC controls and local log retention into your SIEM. We'll include the SAML config examples.
5:45 Tomás Rivera: For the pilot, we want to run a synthetic workload that mirrors our per-tenant QPS distribution. Marcus you mentioned a benchmarking checklist?
5:54 Marcus Lee: Yes, Diane has a template. It includes traffic shape, warm/cold cache runs, context length sweeps, and payload size metrics. We'll send that. Also include an example LangChain test harness.
6:08 Priya Menon: About LangChain/LlamaIndex: do you recommend embedding at the gateway or inside our app? We want to keep embedding pipeline close to data and avoid duplicate calls.
6:20 Marcus Lee: Embeddings are often computed once upstream and then stored in your vector DB. For inference, if you need on-demand embedding, you can call Redwood embeddings. For RAG we recommend precompute for high QPS tenants and do short re-embed windows for freshness. LangChain/LlamaIndex helpers can live in your application layer or in the sidecar depending on topology.
6:41 Tomás Rivera: Any gotchas on model pinning and rollouts? We want to avoid regressions when you update an upstream model variant.
6:48 Diane Huang: We have model version pinning and can do canary rollouts at route level. We also offer quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. That can trigger automatic fallback to a pinned variant if new quality falls below threshold.
7:04 Jared Kwan: Network setup: if we go Dedicated in eu-west, is there a peering option or do we use public endpoints? We prefer private connectivity to avoid egress charges.
7:15 Marcus Lee: There are VPC peering and private link options with cloud providers and direct interconnect partners for Dedicated customers. For Hosted, private link is an enterprise feature. We'll include the network diagram in the security packet.
7:26 Elena Park: Would the security docs include incident response timelines and SOC2 artifact listing?
7:31 Diane Huang: Yes, the pack has SOC2 report summary, controls mapping, incident response runbook high level, and contact SLAs. For Private installs you get more detailed evidence items.
7:42 Tomás Rivera: What about cost controls? We need per-tenant budgets and kill-switches when a tenant unexpectedly spikes.
7:49 Marcus Lee: Two-layer approach: your gateway enforces immediate budget ceilings and token limits (hard stops), and Redwood enforces route-level throttles. We also have webhooks and alerting for budget thresholds. For Dedicated pilots we'll help configure sensible defaults.
8:06 Priya Menon: We run heavy embeddings overnight, and generation during day. Can you recommend autoscaling/bursting policy?
8:14 Marcus Lee: For Dedicated you can set autoscale policies with guaranteed baseline nodes and burst pools for short windows. For hosted, we handle scaling but register burst limits; you'd want a high-priority plan for production.
8:24 Arielle Gomez: Quick recap — HelioForge wants: 1) pilot on Dedicated for EU latency/residency, 2) sample LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter and test harness, 3) security pack, 4) pricing & pilot SOW. We'll deliver those. Anything to add?
8:40 Tomás Rivera: Also include recommended quota architecture for per-tenant enforcement — example with sidecar vs central gateway pros/cons.
8:48 Arielle Gomez: Noted. Any final questions?
8:52 Priya Menon: Small one — do you have example code for low-latency streaming responses with function-calls? We're trying to implement progressive rendering in the UI.
8:58 Marcus Lee: Yes, we have streaming SDK examples and function-calling templates; they show chunked responses and a confirmed ordering strategy. We'll include a small react example.
9:10 Elena Park: For the pilot, security will do a short questionnaire. Expect a list of ~30-40 items.
9:16 Diane Huang: We'll help fill high-level items and give contact for third-party review.
9:21 Tomás Rivera: Cool. Let's schedule the pilot kickoff week of 4/22.
9:24 Arielle Gomez: Great, I'll send calendar invites and the follow-ups. Thanks everyone.
9:29 [meeting ends]
questions: Can Redwood do per-tenant token quotas and throttling?
What observability hooks exist for token-level metrics and exporting traces?
What are the latency expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted for short prompts?
What network options (VPC peering/privatelink) exist for Dedicated/Hosted?
